questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question:
A metal piece of mass 420 g present at 80°C is dropped in 80g of water present at 20°C in a calorimeter of mass 84g. If the final temperature of the mixture is 30°C, then calculate the specific heat capacity of the metal piece.
[Specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹ (= 4200 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹), Specific heat capacity of the calorimeter = 200 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹ (= 0.2 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹)]
questions.solution: Heat lost by metal = 420 x S x 50 = 21000 S J. Heat gained by water = 80 x 4.2 x 10 = 3360 J. Heat gained by calorimeter = 84 x 0.2 x 10 = 168 J. Heat lost = heat gained: 21000 S = 3360 + 168 = 3528, so S = 0.168 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹ (= 168 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹).

marking_points.point: Principle: heat lost by metal = heat gained by water + calorimeter
Heat lost by metal 420 x S x 50; gained by water 80 x 4.2 x 10 and calorimeter 84 x 0.2 x 10
Equation 21000 S = 3528
S = 0.168 J g-1 °C-1 with unit

questions.question:
Rohit playing a flute and Anita playing a piano emit sounds of same pitch and loudness.
(b) If now the loudness of the sound from flute becomes four times that of the sound from piano, then write the value of the ratio AF : AP (AF – amplitude of sound wave from flute, AP – amplitude of sound wave from piano)
questions.solution: Loudness is proportional to (amplitude)^2, so LF/LP = AF^2/AP^2 = 4/1, hence AF : AP = 2 : 1.

marking_points.point: Loudness proportional to amplitude squared, 4/1 = AF^2/AP^2

Rohit playing a flute and Anita playing a piano emit sounds of same pitch and loudness.
(c) Define 'Pitch' of a sound.
questions.solution: Pitch is the sensation (characteristic) of sound by which a note is judged shrill (high) or flat (low); it depends on frequency. High pitch corresponds to high frequency and low pitch to low frequency.

marking_points.point: Pitch is the characteristic/sensation of a sound distinguishing shrill from flat
Depends on frequency (higher frequency = higher pitch)

questions.question: (a) Name two factors on which the force experienced by a conductor carrying current, placed in a magnetic field, depends. Also, state how these factors affect the force.
questions.solution: Factors: strength of the magnetic field and strength of the current flowing. Force is directly proportional to the strength of the magnetic field; force is directly proportional to the strength of the current.

marking_points.point: Factor 1: magnetic field strength, force directly proportional
Factor 2: current strength, force directly proportional

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: (b) With the help of which rule you can determine the direction of force acting on a current carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field?

answer_items.prompt: Rule for direction of force on a current-carrying conductor

questions.solution: Fleming's left-hand rule: with thumb, first finger and second finger of the left hand mutually perpendicular, the thumb gives the direction of force, the first finger the direction of the magnetic field and the second finger the direction of current.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question:
If a wire of resistance 2 ohm gets stretched to thrice its original length:
(a) Calculate the new resistance of the wire.
questions.solution: R = rho l/A. New length 3l, so new area A/3 (volume constant). R' = rho(3l)/(A/3) = 9R = 9 x 2 = 18 ohm.

marking_points.point: Length becomes 3l and area becomes A/3
R' = 9R = 18 ohm with unit

marking_points.point: Remains unchanged
Reason: depends on material, not dimensions
